entities.summary:
Diomede Carafa (1492–1560) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal. He played a key role in the Council of Trent, where he advocated for reforms aimed at strengthening the Catholic Church's response to Protestantism.

As a prominent cleric, Diomede Carafa held significant influence within the Vatican during a tumultuous period in European history. His efforts contributed to the development of the Tridentine Mass and the reorganization of the Church's hierarchy.

The legacy of Diomede Carafa can be seen in the continued relevance of the Council of Trent's reforms, which have shaped Catholic theology and practice to this day. His influence extends beyond the realm of religious politics, as well, with his work reflecting broader societal shifts during the Renaissance.

A testament to the enduring impact of his efforts is the ongoing presence of Tridentine Masses in some Catholic traditions, a direct result of Diomede Carafa's tireless advocacy for reform.
